The column-1 cap forces exactly 2 starts (exiting column 2 at the top or bottom), and by symmetry the column-$n$ cap likewise forces the path to enter/exit column $n-1$ at opposite ends before stepping into $B=(2,n-1)$. 

For the interior columns $3,\dots,n-2$, the path must snake through each $3\times 1$ slice. At each such column there are exactly 3 admissible local routings consistent with a single spanning path (the three cyclic shifts of the vertical “U-turn” pattern), and these choices are independent from column to column. Hence for $n\ge 5$ the recurrence is $H(n)=3\,H(n-1)$.

With $H(4)=2$ we get $H(n)=2\cdot 3^{\,n-4}$. For the $3\times 10$ grid ($n=10$),
$$H(10)=2\cdot 3^{6}=2\cdot 729=1458.$$

\boxed{1458}
